purpose: General principles for writing design documents (the How) when no project-specific rules exist: scope, prohibited content, judgment criteria, architecture norms, and a severity catalog.
summary: Definition of a design document: responsibility, what not to write, lifetime, and revision via additive development
Prohibited content such as bulk source code, unjustified technology choices, and out-of-requirement features
Handling of quantitative goals: no guarantee statements and no AI-guessed targets
Judgment criterion: can an implementer implement from this document
Hierarchical splitting guidance, optional sections, and Mermaid diagram guidelines
No history sections; maintenance rule to report design-implementation mismatches to the user
Norms for architecture dependency direction, responsibility separation and cohesion, and availability and SPOF, with gray-zone tolerances
Severity catalog mapping violations to critical, major, or minor, including deliverables and additive-feature frontmatter
tasks: Deciding whether content belongs in a design document or requirements
Splitting a large design into parent and child documents
Judging severity of design review findings
Updating a design document after implementation changes
Defining error handling and SPOF design
title: 設計書 作成原則
